newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were unchanged with a slightly better tone early Friday, though traders said activity levels were barely registering.

"It's a summer Friday," one trader said. He added that that market participants were glad to see gross domestic product revisions come in as expected, but that had been about the only focus for the day.

The markets showed little reaction after the Commerce Department said it revised the first quarter GDP figure to up 5.9 percent from the 5.8 percent originally reported. The revision was in line with economists forecasts.
After the data, the benchmark 30-year government bond was up 4/32 at 98-4/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
The University of Michigan's final June consumer confidence report is set for release at 1000 EDT. Economists expect the figure to show a reading of 103.5, compared to 103.2 in the previous report.
In debt futures, the September muni contract was up 8/32 at 116-27/32. The September T-bond contract also gained 8/32 to 111-13/32. The MOB spread was unchanged from Thursday at 174 ticks.
In secondary trading, bids on Delaware River Port Authority FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 were up 1/4 at 99. Loyola University, Ill., MBIA 5.0s of 2024 were two basis points higher at 5.70 percent.

Preliminary supply tallies for next week's holiday-shortened session show just $740 million on the calendar. The largest issue so far is a $140.5 million competitive offering from Mississippi on Tuesday.
